# Workflow Overview

GitHub Actions separates pull-request validation, validation of `develop`, nightly publication, release packaging, and storage cleanup. The [workflow files](workflows/) are the source of truth for triggers, job dependencies, permissions, and implementation details.

## Workflows

| Workflow | Trigger | Purpose and main elements |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Feature - Sanity check](workflows/branch.yml) | Pull requests targeting `develop` | Validates the pull-request head with a Linux Docker build and automated tests, and containerized directory backend tests against the Firestore emulator. `Feature Ready` depends only on the Linux job. |
| [macOS - Native builds](workflows/macos-build.yml) | Reusable workflow call | Builds, tests, and packages separate experimental Apple Silicon and Intel x86_64 applications at the requested source SHA. Used by develop validation and nightly publication. |
| [Linux ARM64 - Pi 5 candidate](workflows/arm64.yml) | Reusable call from Develop - Sanity, or manual dispatch | Native ARM64 Docker compilation, hardware-AES known-answer and existing CTests using the default `gl1` renderer. Uploads a separate architecture-labelled candidate. Software-rendered CI does not certify Pi 5 V3D, peripherals, performance or independent crypto review. |
| [Develop - Build Container Image](workflows/develop-build-image.yml) | Reusable workflow call or manual dispatch | Publishes Linux and Windows cross-compilation build images to GHCR. Commit-specific images connect validation and nightly packaging to the same source revision; `develop` image tags support consumers of the current development environment. |
| [Develop - Sanity](workflows/develop.yml) | Push to `develop` | Publishes build images, runs a Linux build with automated tests and a main-menu smoke check, and performs a Debug compilation as the lint-equivalent check. Also runs native Windows transport CTests, the experimental macOS build/tests/package, and the ARM64 candidate workflow. All checks must pass to advance `sanity` and enable the nightly scheduler. |
| [Develop - Nightly Scheduler](workflows/develop-nightly-scheduler.yml) | Every four hours while enabled, or manual dispatch | Requests a nightly build from `sanity` and disables itself until a later successful develop validation enables it again. |
| [Develop - Nightly](workflows/develop-nightly.yml) | Dispatch from the `sanity` tag | Packages Linux and Windows runtime files from the captured validated commit using its matching build images, without rerunning their application tests. Builds the macOS package at the same SHA. Publishes the existing combined ZIP and separate macOS assets as the current `nightly` release. Then builds and deploys the directory image from that SHA to staging. |
| [Directory - Production promotion](workflows/directory-production.yml) | Push to `master` | Deploys the last successfully verified staging directory image by digest, without rebuilding it. Does not change game packaging. |
| [Release Artifact](workflows/master-release.yml) | Push to `master` or manual dispatch | Builds and packages a combined Linux and Windows runtime artifact using the `develop` build images. GitHub release asset publication is conditional on a tag-based invocation. |
| [Storage Cleanup](workflows/storage-cleanup.yml) | Weekly schedule or manual dispatch | Retains current GHCR build images and removes eligible old versions. Manual runs can also remove exact-name legacy Actions artifacts. |

## Pipeline concept

- Pull-request checks validate proposed changes with Linux/Docker only. Automatic Windows, macOS, and ARM64 verification runs after integration into `develop`, not as a pre-review or pre-merge gate.
- Develop validation establishes the `sanity` checkpoint. Nightly packaging uses that exact source revision and its build images, rather than whichever commit is newest when packaging runs.
- The scheduler separates successful validation from publication. The `nightly` tag and release represent the latest published nightly bundle, not a history of nightly releases. Replacement is non-transactional, so publication can temporarily leave the release unavailable.
- The `master` release-artifact path is separate from nightly publication. It produces a downloadable workflow artifact; a branch push does not itself publish a GitHub release.
- Directory deployment is separate from game hosting. Nightly staging and master promotion use one deployment queue and separate database/runtime identities. See [directory deployment operations](../docs/directory-cloud-run.md).
- Distribution builds select the directory through `D6R_DIRECTORY_DEFAULT_URL`. Nightly uses `https://staging.duel.netusite.cz` on Linux, Windows, and macOS. The existing Linux/Windows release workflow uses `https://duel.netusite.cz`, including manual release runs. There is no macOS caller in that release workflow. Channel selection is independent of build optimization. Other builds have no compiled default. Candidate directory checks use `run.app`; serving checks use the corresponding custom domain before staging eligibility or production success.

## Basic elements and workspace context

- **Containerized execution:** Linux builds and Windows cross-compilation use Docker build environments. Native Windows transport checks exercise the Windows implementation in a native Windows container.
- **Runners and images:** Self-hosted runners handle pull-request Linux validation, develop builds, and nightly work. GitHub-hosted runners support image publication, native Windows checks, scheduling, tagging, release-artifact builds, and storage cleanup. GHCR stores the reusable build images.
- **Artifacts and diagnostics:** Validation diagnostics, smoke evidence, and master transport artifacts are retained for seven days; nightly transport remains at one day. Global CTest logs are always preserved after a test failure. Per-test logs and screenshots are collected only for mapped failed tests, and graphical harnesses explicitly record their full-frame screenshot provenance. Only those recorded PNGs are retained, so comparison crops, normalized images, row/control extracts, and other generated derivatives are excluded regardless of filename.
- **Self-hosted Docker workspace contract:** The runner checkout and Docker daemon can occupy different filesystem namespaces, so the checkout path is not assumed to exist on the daemon host. The [workspace helper](../docker/run-with-daemon-workspace.sh) transfers source and build output through the Docker API. This relies on Docker daemon access and storage for the transferred workspace and output; a shared host path is not required.
- **Directory backend:** The Linux pull-request job builds the [verification container](../services/directory/README.md) from a Docker build context, without a checkout bind mount. Firebase CLI runs the application tests against the local Firestore emulator with a demo project and no cloud credentials. No deployment runs in this workflow.
- **Native dependencies:** Pull-request Linux validation builds its tool image from the checkout. Linux, MinGW and native MSVC use the same [pinned private Mbed TLS configuration](../docker/mbedtls/README.md). The native Windows container builds its static dependency after mounted MSVC setup; the existing native CTests remain required by Develop - Sanity. Directory HTTPS uses separate libcurl builds. Windows bundle packaging follows transitive DLL imports; Mbed TLS is static and its license is included in both bundles.

## Experimental macOS build and nightly

- The [macOS contract](../docs/macos.md) defines Apple Silicon macOS 14+ and Intel x86_64 macOS 13 Ventura+, Release, `gl1`, local play, and the approved Host, direct Join, and Browse IPv4 networking scope. The native execution exception includes automated network verification on each architecture. Linux and Windows keep their existing Docker paths.
- The reusable build uses separate native jobs: ARM64 on `macos-14` and Intel x86_64 on `macos-15-intel`. The ARM64 image retires on **2026-11-02**. Its replacement remains a separate follow-up. The application and all bundled dependencies must preserve the target minimum: macOS 14.0 for ARM64 and macOS 13.0 Ventura for Intel. A newer build host does not change that minimum. Changing only the application deployment target is not sufficient.
- Homebrew installs CMake, Ninja, pkg-config, Python 3.13, SDL2 and its image, mixer and TTF libraries, GLEW, and `openssl@3`. After these prerequisites, CI runs `D6R_MACOS_ARCH=<architecture> bash macos/prepare-runtime-dependencies.sh`. This [dependency helper](../macos/prepare-runtime-dependencies.sh) must select Intel Ventura or ARM64 Sonoma runtime bottles and their dependency closure. Missing compatible bottles must fail preparation rather than select a newer-only dependency.
- The [native build helper](../macos/build.sh) owns application tests, package checks, and dependency bundling. CI sets `D6R_MACOS_ARCH` to `arm64` or `x86_64` and invokes `D6R_SOURCE_REVISION="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" bash macos/build.sh` after dependency preparation. Package checks must enforce the architecture and its minimum macOS version for every bundled binary. Bottle selection alone is not runtime compatibility evidence.
- The helper builds static Mbed TLS 3.6.7 from the [common pinned recipe](../docker/mbedtls/CMakeLists.txt) with the private hardware-only AES profile. Directory HTTPS uses a separate private shared libcurl 8.21.0 from [the source-pinned recipe](../macos/build-curl.sh), not the Homebrew libcurl keg. The recipe verifies archive SHA-256 `ad6f2f94934b38e31e48272833c99b891d045b4565fe942a53fbd27bd3910e16`, uses Homebrew OpenSSL, and enables Apple SecTrust and threaded asynchronous DNS without a CA bundle, CA path, or OpenSSL CA fallback. Both private dependency builds use the selected native SDK, target architecture, and its deployment target (14.0 for ARM64; 13.0 for Intel). The helper selects the private curl headers and dylib explicitly and records its configuration and identity in dependency build metadata.
- Keep certificate-chain and hostname verification enabled. Native trust checks must observe actual SecTrust evaluation; an HTTPS success with zero observed native evaluations is not proof of Apple system trust. The package must include the non-system dependency closure and licenses without a dependency on build-machine Homebrew paths.
- The reusable workflow passes `directory_default_url` to the helper as `D6R_DIRECTORY_DEFAULT_URL`. The helper must pass it to the same CMake option. The default is empty for develop validation and other unchannelled builds; the nightly caller supplies staging. A release-channel invocation must supply `https://duel.netusite.cz`; it must not infer the channel from `Release` optimization.
- Each job produces `build/macos/Duel 6 Reloaded.app` and `build/macos/duel6r-macos-<architecture>.zip` with its `.sha256` file. ARM64 keeps `build-info.json`; Intel supplies `build-info-x86_64.json` in the same output directory. CI transfers the archive and metadata, not the unarchived application. Package and CTest diagnostic artifact names include the architecture. Develop validation artifacts last seven days. Nightly transport artifacts last one day. Failed CTest logs from `build/macos-build/Testing/Temporary/LastTest.log` last seven days.
- Develop validation builds the integrated push SHA. Nightly builds use the captured `sanity` SHA for every platform. Publication waits for the existing Linux/Windows package and both macOS packages. The release retains `duel6r-nightly.zip`, `duel6r-macos-arm64.zip`, `duel6r-macos-arm64.zip.sha256`, and `build-info.json`. It adds `duel6r-macos-x86_64.zip`, `duel6r-macos-x86_64.zip.sha256`, and `build-info-x86_64.json`.
- No Apple signing identity, notarization credentials, or new repository secrets are required. The macOS artifact is experimental unsigned distribution, not verified platform support. Use the artifact's launch instructions and macOS approval procedure; do not disable system-wide security protections.
- Native automated transport, security, process, build, and package verification runs on both architectures after integration in Develop - Sanity at the push SHA. It must pass before `sanity` advances and the nightly scheduler is enabled; it is not a pre-review or pre-merge gate. Use the existing Mac job and application-owned CTest registration. Skipped, Linux-only, or other-architecture results do not establish native behavior for an architecture. No separate readiness workflow is required.
- The user performs actual Mac GUI and live cross-OS verification on both architectures after merge and the subsequent nightly publication, including manual launch, gameplay, saved-data, and visual checks. These checks are deferred, not passed. Native CLI results do not prove Finder launch, input, audio, rendering, graphical host/join, or live cross-OS gameplay. Actual release-asset evidence follows publication.

## Storage cleanup safeguards

- Scheduled runs apply GHCR cleanup; manual runs default to a dry run. The workflow fully inventories both packages and resolves `develop`, `sanity`, and `nightly` before deleting anything, then keeps the newest 10 versions plus protected mutable or exact-SHA tags.
- GHCR cleanup needs `contents: read`, `packages: write`, and repository package Admin access to `duel6r/build` and `duel6r/build-w64`. Ref, inventory, metadata, authentication, or authorization failures stop cleanup.
- Legacy Actions artifact cleanup is manual-only, defaults to `skip`, requires `actions: write`, fully paginates the inventory, and deletes only the exact legacy names listed in the workflow. It does not delete current transport artifacts, diagnostics, smoke evidence, Docker build records, or release assets.

This overview describes the pipeline's responsibilities and relationships, not procedures for implementing individual steps.
